First listed 2026-05-13 · episode or wrap

Conspiracy of Credit Part 1

Eisman places private credit in an early contraction phase, emphasizing redemption pressure, software concentration, bank links and life-insurer exposure. Blue Owl filings confirm striking tender demand, and supervisory evidence supports stronger bank capital. However, gross redemption requests do not equal forced asset sales or net outflows. Claims that virtually all post-2008 lending growth was private, all subprime mortgages were securitized, and rates fell in 2018 are overstated or wrong. The aggregate CDO multiplier and software exposure require tighter definitions. His smaller-than-2008 crisis thesis remains unresolved, with explicit insurer caveats.

Substack · 2026-05-13 ↗
The episode identifies meaningful liquidity and concentration vulnerabilities but blends supported examples with universal claims and stock-flow confusion. Preserve the cautious systemic comparison and separate a sector credit cycle from an economy-wide credit-led recession. Captions contain genuine incomplete sentences; no missing AI prediction is reconstructed.

substack-202888778-c038 · explanation

Previously diverse exposures may become highly correlated, with standard deviation approaching one.

Mixed
Source · 15:58-16:21 ↗
SpeakerSteve Eisman
Stanceasserted
Horizonnot stated
Materialitymajor

The common-exposure warning is valid, but standard deviation is not correlation and approaching one has no universal diversification meaning.

Conditional reasoning

Correlation is covariance divided by the product of standard deviations and ranges from -1 to 1. Standard deviation changes with units: multiplying returns by 100 multiplies it by 100 without changing correlation. Thus standard deviation approaching 1 cannot establish near-perfect correlation.

Assessment test: Estimate covariance and correlation rather than using a unit-dependent volatility threshold.

Evidence and assessment details

Attribution confidence: high. Assessment confidence: medium. Thesis family: correlation-versus-volatility.

No independent empirical outcome evidence is attached. A principle, disclosure or unfinished forecast is not a verified investment win.

How he reasons here

  • Separate sector credit cycles from recession causes.
  • Measure net outflows and liquidity resources alongside gross tender requests.
  • Trace bank financing of ostensibly nonbank credit.
  • Compare common borrower exposures rather than labels.
  • Use consistent stocks, flows, notionals and net losses.
  • Stress insurer liabilities and assets together.
  • Treat ratings as opinions and test shared assumptions independently.
